definitions.explanation: A male child in relation to their parents. This is the neutral/humble form used when referring to one's own son.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}は{大学生|だいがくせい}です。
examples.english: My son is a university student.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}が{二人|ふたり}います。
{息子|むすこ}は{来年|らいねん}{結婚|けっこん}します。
examples.english: My son will get married next year.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}は{今|いま}{高校生|こうこうせい}です。
examples.english: My son is currently a high school student.

examples.japanese: {息子|むすこ}さんは{何歳|なんさい}ですか。
examples.notes: 息子さん is used when referring to someone else's son

notes: {息子|むすこ} is the humble term used when referring to your own son. When referring to someone else's son politely, use {息子|むすこ}さん. The kanji {息|いき} means 'breath' and {子|こ} means 'child', together suggesting 'the child of one's life/breath'.
